items.title: How we save entry-level UX work that teaches craft in the time of AI
items.excerpt: Patrick Neeman argues that AI now does the transcript tagging, theming and clipping juniors used to learn on, and proposes seven tasks UX teams should keep for humans to build the design bench for 2030.

items.title: Figma's Dev Mode MCP Server Explained — and Why It Won't Build You a Website or App
items.excerpt: Explains what Figma's Dev Mode MCP server actually hands to coding agents (design context, variables, component mappings) and why it is a design-to-code bridge, not an app builder.

items.title: Designing an AI Photo Editor Around a Capability Contract
items.excerpt: A product-design case study on structuring an AI photo editor's small upload-prompt-generate interface around an explicit 'capability contract' so users know what the model can and cannot do.

items.title: AtomCut made its own intro using Opus 5.5 ( Launch Motion design )
items.excerpt: AtomCut shows a launch motion-design intro built entirely by Claude Opus 5.5 driving its AtomCut MCP, an example of agent-generated motion graphics.

items.title: Google Stitch Uses Gemini 3.8 Flash to Turn Brand Assets Into UI Designs - Techgenyz
items.excerpt: Google Stitch now uses Gemini 3.8 Flash to read dropped-in brand kits and product shots, auto-extract a design system and styling, and generate brand-consistent marketing and product page layouts.

items.title: "We have the kind of stuff AI wishes it could make": Why trust is more important than ever for the NASA brand
items.excerpt: NASA creative director David Rager on keeping the agency's brand trustworthy when AI-generated imagery floods the feed, and why authentic assets are now a design advantage.

items.title: No, that Apple Games advert isn't AI, and the brilliant BTS video proves it
items.excerpt: Viewers assumed Apple's Games ad was AI-generated; a behind-the-scenes video shows painstaking hand-made stop-motion, highlighting how AI suspicion now shapes how craft is received.

items.title: Pixel Canary is now available in stealth for free on AI Gateway
items.excerpt: Vercel AI Gateway adds Pixel Canary, a stealth model pitched for coding, frontend development and mobile app design, free to use while in stealth.

items.title: You Can Edit Your Photos With Lightroom and Photoshop Inside Google Gemini
items.excerpt: Adobe's Photoshop and Lightroom editing tools now run inside Google Gemini, letting users make color, lighting and retouching edits to photos conversationally without opening Adobe apps.

items.title: New Google Flow build now points to Nano Banana 2.1
items.excerpt: A new Google Flow web build labels an upcoming image model as Nano Banana 2.1, replacing an earlier 2.5 Flash reference; Google has not announced it yet.

items.title: Blender always scared me, but Claude helped me make this animated video in just a few hours
items.excerpt: A Blender novice uses Claude to drive Blender and produce a short 3D animated video in a few hours, showing how AI assistants lower the barrier to 3D tools.

items.title: Engram is a sampler that turns broken AI hallucinations into music
items.excerpt: Thoughtful Things' Engram is a hardware sampler, a 'field recorder for latent space' that circuit-bends tiny on-device AI models into instruments; launching on Kickstarter.

items.title: Tesla’s Optimus robot is going through growing pains
items.excerpt: Tesla's Optimus humanoid is ramping production but its dexterous hands remain the design bottleneck, with supplier and engineering problems slowing the rollout.

items.title: Humanoid robots are getting even creepier (this one can cry on command) - Engadget
items.excerpt: Humanoid robots such as the Yansyn-X2 are being designed to mimic human emotion, including crying on command, raising uncanny-valley questions for robot product design.

items.title: Researchers plug GPT-6 Astra directly into a robot and let it clean up an unfamiliar kitchen
items.excerpt: Stanford and Caltech's HomeBody system lets GPT-6 Astra call modular robot skills directly, and a humanoid independently tidied an unfamiliar kitchen without a trained control layer.

items.title: Hologram: Meta Is Finally Set To Ship Realistic Avatars, And We Tried Them
items.excerpt: Meta set a timeline to ship its realistic 'Hologram' avatars, shoulders-up on Ray-Ban Display then full-body on its VR Glasses; UploadVR tried both at Connect.

items.title: The AI transformation underway at Musinsa
items.excerpt: How Korean fashion platform Musinsa's two directors run an organization-level AX program, moving beyond individual ChatGPT proficiency to restyling how teams work with AI.

items.title: I stopped asking my team to use AI. I asked them to manage it
items.excerpt: A leader explains shifting teams from 'use AI' mandates to managing AI agents as teammates with defined roles, reviews and human oversight.
